    3. If the current range partially overlaps with the target range, it calculates the midpoint `mid` of the current range.
    4. It recursively calls itself with the left sub-range `[l, mid)` using `i << 1` as the new index.
    5. It recursively calls itself with the right sub-range `[mid + 1, r)` using `i << 1 | 1` as the new index (bug is here).
]
